src/infrastructure/http/routes/userRoutes.ts: `export function userRoutes(deps: Dependencies): Router` builds `new UserController(new CreateUserUseCase(deps.users, deps.ids))` and registers `router.post('/users', controller.create)`.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one job: building Express routers. All three files use the same factory shape. Each takes `deps: Dependencies` and builds its use cases from the injected ports. It then passes those use cases to one controller, registers that controller's handlers on a new Router and returns the Router. No file reaches past its controller to handle requests itself, puts business rules in a handler or repeats an invariant. Building use cases inside each route factory is a deliberate, consistent wiring pattern, not a bypass. `taskRoutes` serves the nested `/projects/:projectId/tasks` paths. That is ordinary REST nesting for the task resource and does not duplicate anything in `projectRoutes`, which only handles `POST /projects`.
